title: Your guide to installing solar energy for off-grid buildings (Cabin Solar in Nunavut)
label: Installing off-grid solar power (Cabin Solar guide)
licence: No licence or copyright statement in the PDF (free download; owner assumes full permission, 19 Nov 2026)
notes: 61 pages, real text. Written by Andrew Cahill (Relay Education, a renewable-energy education charity) for the Arctic Renewables Society's cabin solar course; funded by the Government of Canada (CIRNAC Northern REACHE); hosted on the Government of Nunavut's climate-change site. Step by step for a small off-grid system: electricity basics, panels, batteries (flooded and sealed lead-acid, lithium iron phosphate, depth of discharge, cold), charge controller, inverter, load worksheet, days of autonomy, battery sizing, DC breakers and fuses, cable sizes, wall and roof mounting step by step, grounding, switching on and off, maintenance, troubleshooting, winter storage, when to replace batteries. Spot-checked 21 Nov 2026: fuse and breaker rule (25% above the maximum current, DC-rated only), cable ampacity table and LFP cold warnings are sound. One caveat: between panels and controller, US and IEC rules size the protection at about 1.56 x the panels' short-circuit current; the guide's 1.25 x can cause nuisance trips, not a fire risk. Cable sizes are American (AWG); in France buy the next metric size up: 10 AWG = 6 mm2, 6 AWG = 16 mm2, 4 AWG = 25 mm2, 2/0 AWG = 70 mm2. It cites the Canadian Electrical Code and Nunavut grants (ignore those parts). Job: primary for solar electricity and batteries (E1). Chosen over NRCan Photovoltaic Systems: A Buyer's Guide (2002, before lithium batteries) and the SEIAPI/PPA Off Grid PV design guidelines (2012; tropical, installer checklist, and its PDF text layer is garbled). sha-256 (two identical downloads, 21 Nov 2026): ba7c768125bc8a290d5478ed10046bba8fea7d7d7d063003e031a9787a5d7971.
